newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK tax experts dub '97 budget "disappointment".
newsitem.headline: HK tax experts dub '97 budget "disappointment".

text.p: Tax experts in Hong Kong said on Wednesday they were "disappointed" with Financial Secretary Donald Tsang's 1997/98 budget, which did nothing to boost the territory's competitiveness.
"Across the board, he hasn't done anything which could help boost Hong Kong's competitive edge," Christina Lam, tax partner of Arthur Anderson, told Reuters.

She said Tsang needed to do a lot more to maintain Hong Kong's position in the region, but understood that his prudent approach in the 1997/98 budget was due to the sovereignty transfer later this year.
Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1.

"We understand why he is doing this for this year. But maybe next year onwards he has to put a lot of effort into introducing more across-the-board incentives and focusing on tax issues to help Hong Kong's competitiveness," Lam said.

"In order to maintain our competitiveness, not just for the next year, but into the next millenium, we believe he should consider some sort of move, such as reduction of corporate profit tax," she said.
Joseph Wong, tax partner at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu, also expressed disappointment, saying Tsang did little to help Hong Kong's economy.
"We believe the government should take more active steps in boosting the economy," Wong said.
He called for more tax incentives along with a cut in corporate profits taxes, but welcomed the Financial Secretary's hands-off approach to booming property prices beyond increasing land supply.
